facts.text: Granville was founded in 1805 by settlers from Granville, Massachusetts, making it a planned community unlike many early Ohio towns.
Denison University sits on a hill overlooking the village; it began in 1831 as the Granville Theological and Literary Seminary.
The Alligator Effigy Mound, built by Fort Ancient people between 800-1200 CE, sits in Granville and is listed on the National Register.
Granville’s first school opened in January 1806, just two months after the first settlers arrived.
The village’s historic Infirmary Mound Park is named for a prehistoric mound on its grounds and is managed by the Licking Park District.
Granville once served as an alternate route on the Underground Railroad, offering a safer path when main routes through Columbus were too dangerous.
